204	/-! ## §3. The kernel–pullback comparison map -/
205	
206	/-- **The kernel–pullback comparison map** `g'^*(ker q) ⟶ ker (g'^* q)`
207	(the abstract `CategoryTheory.Limits.kernelComparison` at the module pullback
208	functor; the pullback preserves zero morphisms, being a left adjoint —
209	`Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction` — between abelian categories).
210	It is characterised by `κ ≫ ker(g'^*q).ι = g'^*(ker q .ι)`
211	(`kernelComparison_comp_ι`).  `Scheme.Modules.pullback_kernel_isLocallyTrivial`
212	(blueprint `lem:relative_divisor_base_change`) proves it is an isomorphism
213	when the cokernel of `ker q ⟶ E` is flat over the base of a cartesian
214	square. -/
215	noncomputable def Modules.pullbackKernelComparison
216	    {X' X : Scheme.{u}} (g' : X' ⟶ X) {E F : X.Modules} (q : E ⟶ F) :
217	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback g').obj (Limits.kernel q) ⟶
218	      Limits.kernel ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g').map q) :=
219	  kernelComparison q (Scheme.Modules.pullback g')
220	
221	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
222	lemma Modules.pullbackKernelComparison_comp_ι
223	    {X' X : Scheme.{u}} (g' : X' ⟶ X) {E F : X.Modules} (q : E ⟶ F) :
224	    Modules.pullbackKernelComparison g' q ≫
225	        Limits.kernel.ι ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g').map q) =
226	      (Scheme.Modules.pullback g').map (Limits.kernel.ι q) :=
227	  kernelComparison_comp_ι q (Scheme.Modules.pullback g')

229	/-- **The kernel–pullback comparison is an epimorphism whenever `q` is an
230	epimorphism.**  This is the categorical (right-exact) half of the isomorphism
231	claim in `Scheme.Modules.pullback_kernel_isLocallyTrivial`: the module pullback
232	`g'^*` is a left adjoint
233	(`Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction`), hence preserves cokernels, so
234	applied to the short exact sequence `0 → ker q → E → F → 0` (`q` epi, so `F` is
235	the cokernel of `ker q ↪ E`) it stays right exact: `g'^*(ker q) → g'^*E →
236	g'^*F → 0` is exact.  Exactness at `g'^*E` says precisely that the kernel lift
237	`g'^*(ker q) → ker (g'^* q)` — which is `pullbackKernelComparison g' q` — is an
238	epimorphism.  (The remaining monomorphism half is the genuine flat-base-change
239	content, requiring `F` flat over the base, and is handled in
240	`pullback_kernel_isLocallyTrivial`.) -/
241	lemma Modules.epi_pullbackKernelComparison
242	    {X' X : Scheme.{u}} (g' : X' ⟶ X) {E F : X.Modules} (q : E ⟶ F) [Epi q] :
243	    Epi (Modules.pullbackKernelComparison g' q) := by
244	  haveI : PreservesColimitsOfSize.{0, 0} (Scheme.Modules.pullback g') :=
245	    (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction g').leftAdjoint_preservesColimits
246	  have hSG := (CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.exact_kernel q).map_of_epi_of_preservesCokernel
247	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback g') ‹Epi q› inferInstance
248	  exact hSG.epi_kernelLift

250	/-- **Basis-local criterion for monomorphisms of `𝒪_X`-modules.**  If `B` is a basis of
251	opens of `X` and `φ : M ⟶ N` is injective on sections over every basic open `B i`, then
252	`φ` is a monomorphism.  Companion of the basis-local iso criterion
253	`Modules.isIso_of_isIso_app_of_isBasis` (`AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.FlatBaseChange`):
254	basis injectivity gives stalkwise injectivity
255	(`TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor_map_injective_of_isBasis`), hence the underlying morphism of
256	sheaves of abelian groups is a monomorphism (`TopCat.Presheaf.mono_of_stalk_mono`), and the
257	faithful forgetful functor `Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf` reflects it. -/
258	theorem Modules.mono_of_injective_app_of_isBasis {X : Scheme.{u}} {M N : X.Modules}
259	    {ι : Type*} {B : ι → X.Opens} (hB : TopologicalSpace.Opens.IsBasis (Set.range B))
260	    (φ : M ⟶ N) (h : ∀ i, Function.Injective (φ.app (B i))) : Mono φ := by
261	  have happ : ∀ U ∈ Set.range B,
262	      Function.Injective (((Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf X).map φ).app (Opposite.op U)) := by
263	    rintro U ⟨i, rfl⟩; exact h i
264	  have hstalk : ∀ x : X, Function.Injective
265	      ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor Ab.{u} x).map ((Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf X).map φ)) :=
266	    fun x => TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor_map_injective_of_isBasis hB happ x
267	  let MS : TopCat.Sheaf Ab.{u} X := ⟨M.presheaf, M.isSheaf⟩
268	  let NS : TopCat.Sheaf Ab.{u} X := ⟨N.presheaf, N.isSheaf⟩
269	  let fS : MS ⟶ NS := ⟨(Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf X).map φ⟩
270	  haveI : ∀ x, Mono ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor Ab.{u} x).map fS.1) := fun x =>
271	    (AddCommGrpCat.mono_iff_injective _).mpr (hstalk x)
272	  haveI hmS : Mono fS := TopCat.Presheaf.mono_of_stalk_mono fS
273	  haveI : Mono ((Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf X).map φ) :=
274	    (CategoryTheory.Sheaf.Hom.mono_iff_presheaf_mono _ _ fS).mp hmS
275	  exact (Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf X).mono_of_mono_map ‹_›

277	/-- **The kernel–pullback comparison is an isomorphism as soon as `g'^*` keeps
278	the kernel inclusion `ker q ↪ E` monic.**  Combining the always-available
279	epimorphism half (`epi_pullbackKernelComparison`, `q` epi) with the
280	monomorphism half, `X'.Modules` being abelian (hence balanced) upgrades
281	`pullbackKernelComparison g' q` to an isomorphism: `κ` is monic because
282	`κ ≫ ker(g'^*q).ι = g'^*(ker q .ι)` (`pullbackKernelComparison_comp_ι`) is monic
283	(the hypothesis, with `ker(g'^*q).ι` monic), and epi + mono ⟹ iso.
284	
285	This isolates the *entire* remaining content of
286	`Scheme.Modules.pullback_kernel_isLocallyTrivial` into the single flat-base-change
287	fact `Mono (g'^*(ker q .ι))` — that the right-exact pullback preserves the
288	injection `ker q ↪ E` because the cokernel `F` is flat over the base
289	(Stacks 00HL, `Module.Flat.rTensor_injective_of_exact`, affine-locally through the
290	base-change section calculus). -/
291	lemma Modules.isIso_pullbackKernelComparison_of_mono
292	    {X' X : Scheme.{u}} (g' : X' ⟶ X) {E F : X.Modules} (q : E ⟶ F) [Epi q]
293	    (hmono : Mono ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g').map (Limits.kernel.ι q))) :
294	    IsIso (Modules.pullbackKernelComparison g' q) := by
295	  haveI := Modules.epi_pullbackKernelComparison g' q
296	  haveI : Mono (Modules.pullbackKernelComparison g' q ≫
297	      Limits.kernel.ι ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g').map q)) := by
298	    rw [Modules.pullbackKernelComparison_comp_ι]; exact hmono
299	  haveI : Mono (Modules.pullbackKernelComparison g' q) :=
300	    mono_of_mono _ (Limits.kernel.ι ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g').map q))
301	  exact isIso_of_mono_of_epi _

303	/-! ## §4. Shrinking a trivialising chart -/
304	
305	namespace LineBundle
306	
307	/-- **A trivialising chart restricts along any smaller open** (the Stacks
308	01HH chart chase of `IsLocallyTrivial.pullback`, specialised to the open
309	inclusion `V ≤ U`): if `M|_U ≅ 𝒪_U` and `V ≤ U`, then `M|_V ≅ 𝒪_V`.  The
310	witness is the `i1–i7` restriction/pullback chain along
311	`g := X.homOfLE hVU : V ⟶ U` — `g ≫ U.ι = V.ι`, so restriction to `V`
312	factors as pullback along `g` of the restriction to `U`, and the pullback of
313	the unit is the unit (`SheafOfModules.pullbackObjUnitToUnit`, an isomorphism
314	because `Opens.map g.base` is final). -/
315	lemma IsLocallyTrivial.trivialization_of_le {X : Scheme.{u}} {M : X.Modules}
316	    {U V : X.Opens} (hVU : V ≤ U)
317	    (t : M.restrict U.ι ≅ SheafOfModules.unit (U : Scheme).ringCatSheaf) :
318	    Nonempty (M.restrict V.ι ≅ SheafOfModules.unit (V : Scheme).ringCatSheaf) := by
319	  set g : (V : Scheme) ⟶ (U : Scheme) := X.homOfLE hVU with hg_def
320	  have hgι : g ≫ U.ι = V.ι := X.homOfLE_ι hVU
321	  haveI : (TopologicalSpace.Opens.map g.base).Final :=
322	    CategoryTheory.final_of_representablyFlat _
323	  refine ⟨?_⟩
324	  -- 1: M.restrict V.ι ≅ (pullback V.ι).obj M
325	  let i1 := (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctorIsoPullback V.ι).app M
326	  -- 2: ≅ (pullback (g ≫ U.ι)).obj M  (using V.ι = g ≫ U.ι)
327	  let i2 := (Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr hgι.symm).app M
328	  -- 3: ≅ (pullback g).obj ((pullback U.ι).obj M)
329	  let i3 := ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp g U.ι).symm).app M
330	  -- 4: ≅ (pullback g).obj (unit_U)  (restrict back and trivialise)
331	  let i4 := (Scheme.Modules.pullback g).mapIso
332	    ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctorIsoPullback U.ι).symm.app M ≪≫ t)
333	  -- 5: ≅ unit_V  (pullback of the unit is the unit; iso since `Opens.map
334	  -- g.base` is final)
335	  let i5 := asIso (SheafOfModules.pullbackObjUnitToUnit g.toRingCatSheafHom)
336	  exact i1 ≪≫ i2 ≪≫ i3 ≪≫ i4 ≪≫ i5
337	
338	/-- **Chart shrinking**: a locally trivial module has a trivialising *affine*
339	chart inside any open neighbourhood of any point.  Combines the defining
340	chart of `IsLocallyTrivial` with an affine shrink
341	(`exists_isAffineOpen_mem_and_subset`) and the restriction of the
342	trivialisation (`trivialization_of_le`). -/
343	lemma IsLocallyTrivial.exists_affine_trivializing_le
344	    {X : Scheme.{u}} {M : X.Modules} (hM : IsLocallyTrivial M)
345	    {x : X} {W : X.Opens} (hxW : x ∈ W) :
346	    ∃ V : X.Opens, x ∈ V ∧ IsAffineOpen V ∧ V ≤ W ∧
347	      Nonempty (M.restrict V.ι ≅ SheafOfModules.unit (V : Scheme).ringCatSheaf) := by
348	  obtain ⟨U, hxU, hUaff, ⟨t⟩⟩ := hM x
349	  obtain ⟨V, hVaff, hxV, hVle⟩ := exists_isAffineOpen_mem_and_subset

96:/--
97:If a functor `F : C ⥤ D` preserves short exact sequences on the left-hand side, (i.e.
98:if `0 ⟶ A ⟶ B ⟶ C ⟶ 0` is exact then `0 ⟶ F(A) ⟶ F(B) ⟶ F(C)` is exact)
99:then it preserves monomorphism.

101:lemma preservesMonomorphisms_of_preserves_shortExact_left
102:    (h : ∀ (S : ShortComplex C), S.ShortExact → (S.map F).Exact ∧ Mono (F.map S.f)) :
103:    F.PreservesMonomorphisms where
104:  preserves f := h _ { exact := exact_cokernel f } |>.2

106:set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
107:/--
108:For an additive functor `F : C ⥤ D` between abelian categories, the following are equivalent:
109:- `F` preserves short exact sequences on the left-hand side, i.e. if `0 ⟶ A ⟶ B ⟶ C ⟶ 0` is exact
110:  then `0 ⟶ F(A) ⟶ F(B) ⟶ F(C)` is exact.
111:- `F` preserves exact sequences on the left-hand side, i.e. if `A ⟶ B ⟶ C` is exact where `A ⟶ B`
112:  is mono, then `F(A) ⟶ F(B) ⟶ F(C)` is exact and `F(A) ⟶ F(B)` is mono as well.
113:- `F` preserves kernels.
114:- `F` preserves finite limits.
115:-/
116:lemma preservesFiniteLimits_tfae : List.TFAE
117:    [
118:      ∀ (S : ShortComplex C), S.ShortExact → (S.map F).Exact ∧ Mono (F.map S.f),
119:      ∀ (S : ShortComplex C), S.Exact ∧ Mono S.f → (S.map F).Exact ∧ Mono (F.map S.f),
120:      ∀ ⦃X Y : C⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y), PreservesLimit (parallelPair f 0) F,
121:      PreservesFiniteLimits F
122:    ] := by
123:  tfae_have 1 → 2
124:  | hF, S, ⟨hS, hf⟩ => by
125:    have := preservesMonomorphisms_of_preserves_shortExact_left F hF
126:    refine ⟨?_, inferInstance⟩
127:    let T := ShortComplex.mk S.f (Abelian.coimage.π S.g) (Abelian.comp_coimage_π_eq_zero S.zero)
128:    let φ : T.map F ⟶ S.map F :=
129:      { τ₁ := 𝟙 _
130:        τ₂ := 𝟙 _
131:        τ₃ := F.map <| Abelian.factorThruCoimage S.g
132:        comm₂₃ := show 𝟙 _ ≫ F.map _ = F.map (cokernel.π _) ≫ _ by
133:          rw [Category.id_comp, ← F.map_comp, cokernel.π_desc] }
134:    exact (exact_iff_of_epi_of_isIso_of_mono φ).1 (hF T ⟨(S.exact_iff_exact_coimage_π).1 hS⟩).1
135:  tfae_have 2 → 3
136:  | hF, X, Y, f => by
137:    refine preservesLimit_of_preserves_limit_cone (kernelIsKernel f) ?_
138:    apply (KernelFork.isLimitMapConeEquiv _ F).2
139:    let S := ShortComplex.mk _ _ (kernel.condition f)
140:    let hS := hF S ⟨exact_kernel f, inferInstance⟩
141:    have : Mono (S.map F).f := hS.2
142:    exact hS.1.fIsKernel
143:  tfae_have 3 → 4
144:  | hF => by
145:    exact preservesFiniteLimits_of_preservesKernels F
146:  tfae_have 4 → 1
147:  | ⟨_⟩, S, hS =>
148:    (S.map F).exact_and_mono_f_iff_f_is_kernel |>.2 ⟨KernelFork.mapIsLimit _ hS.fIsKernel F⟩
149:  tfae_finish

157:If a functor `F : C ⥤ D` preserves exact sequences on the right-hand side (i.e.
158:if `0 ⟶ A ⟶ B ⟶ C ⟶ 0` is exact then `F(A) ⟶ F(B) ⟶ F(C) ⟶ 0` is exact),

13:/-!
14:# Pullback of presheaves of modules
15:
16:Let `F : C ⥤ D` be a functor, `R : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat` and `S : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat` be presheaves
17:of rings, and `φ : S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R` be a morphism of presheaves of rings,
18:we introduce the pullback functor `pullback : PresheafOfModules S ⥤ PresheafOfModules R`
19:as the left adjoint of `pushforward : PresheafOfModules R ⥤ PresheafOfModules S`.
20:The existence of this left adjoint functor is obtained under suitable universe assumptions.
21:
22:From the compatibility of `pushforward` with respect to composition, we deduce
23:similar pseudofunctor-like properties of the `pullback` functors.
24:
25:-/
26:
27:@[expose] public section
28:
29:universe v v₁ v₂ v₃ v₄ u₁ u₂ u₃ u₄ u
30:
31:open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite Functor
32:
33:namespace PresheafOfModules
34:
35:section
36:
37:variable {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} D]
38:  {F : C ⥤ D} {R : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{u}} {S : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{u}} (φ : S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R)
39:  [(pushforward.{v} φ).IsRightAdjoint]
40:
41:/-- The pullback functor `PresheafOfModules S ⥤ PresheafOfModules R` induced by
42:a morphism of presheaves of rings `S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R`, defined as the left adjoint
43:functor to the pushforward, when it exists. -/
44:noncomputable def pullback : PresheafOfModules.{v} S ⥤ PresheafOfModules.{v} R :=
45:  (pushforward.{v} φ).leftAdjoint
46:
47:/-- Given a morphism of presheaves of rings `S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R`, this is the adjunction
48:between associated pullback and pushforward functors on the categories
49:of presheaves of modules. -/

13:/-!
14:# Pullback of presheaves of modules
15:
16:Let `F : C ⥤ D` be a functor, `R : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat` and `S : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat` be presheaves
17:of rings, and `φ : S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R` be a morphism of presheaves of rings,
18:we introduce the pullback functor `pullback : PresheafOfModules S ⥤ PresheafOfModules R`
19:as the left adjoint of `pushforward : PresheafOfModules R ⥤ PresheafOfModules S`.
20:The existence of this left adjoint functor is obtained under suitable universe assumptions.
21:
22:From the compatibility of `pushforward` with respect to composition, we deduce
23:similar pseudofunctor-like properties of the `pullback` functors.
24:
25:-/
26:
27:@[expose] public section
28:
29:universe v v₁ v₂ v₃ v₄ u₁ u₂ u₃ u₄ u
30:
31:open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite Functor
32:
33:namespace PresheafOfModules
34:
35:section
36:
37:variable {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} D]
38:  {F : C ⥤ D} {R : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{u}} {S : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{u}} (φ : S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R)
39:  [(pushforward.{v} φ).IsRightAdjoint]
40:
41:/-- The pullback functor `PresheafOfModules S ⥤ PresheafOfModules R` induced by
42:a morphism of presheaves of rings `S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R`, defined as the left adjoint
43:functor to the pushforward, when it exists. -/
44:noncomputable def pullback : PresheafOfModules.{v} S ⥤ PresheafOfModules.{v} R :=
45:  (pushforward.{v} φ).leftAdjoint
46:
47:/-- Given a morphism of presheaves of rings `S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R`, this is the adjunction
48:between associated pullback and pushforward functors on the categories
49:of presheaves of modules. -/
50:noncomputable def pullbackPushforwardAdjunction : pullback.{v} φ ⊣ pushforward.{v} φ :=
51:  Adjunction.ofIsRightAdjoint (pushforward φ)
52:
53:/-- Given a morphism of presheaves of rings `φ : S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R`, this is the property
54:that the (partial) left adjoint functor of `pushforward φ` is defined
55:on a certain object `M : PresheafOfModules S`. -/
56:abbrev pullbackObjIsDefined : ObjectProperty (PresheafOfModules.{v} S) :=
57:  (pushforward φ).leftAdjointObjIsDefined
58:
59:end
60:
61:section
62:
63:variable {C D : Type u} [SmallCategory C] [SmallCategory D]
64:  {F : C ⥤ D} {R : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{u}} {S : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{u}} (φ : S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R)
65:
66:/-- Given a morphism of presheaves of rings `φ : S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R`, where `F : C ⥤ D`,
67:`S : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat`, `R : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat` and `X : C`, the (partial) left adjoint
68:functor of `pushforward φ` is defined on the object `(free S).obj (yoneda.obj X)`:
69:this object shall be mapped to `(free R).obj (yoneda.obj (F.obj X))`. -/
70:noncomputable def pushforwardCompCoyonedaFreeYonedaCorepresentableBy (X : C) :
71:    (pushforward φ ⋙ coyoneda.obj (op ((free S).obj (yoneda.obj X)))).CorepresentableBy
72:      ((free R).obj (yoneda.obj (F.obj X))) where
73:  homEquiv {M} := freeYonedaEquiv.trans
74:    (freeYonedaEquiv (M := (pushforward φ).obj M)).symm
75:  homEquiv_comp {M N} g f := freeYonedaEquiv.injective (by
76:    dsimp
77:    erw [Equiv.apply_symm_apply, freeYonedaEquiv_comp]
78:    conv_rhs => erw [freeYonedaEquiv_comp]
79:    erw [Equiv.apply_symm_apply]
80:    rfl)
81:
82:lemma pullbackObjIsDefined_free_yoneda (X : C) :
83:    pullbackObjIsDefined φ ((free S).obj (yoneda.obj X)) :=
84:  (pushforwardCompCoyonedaFreeYonedaCorepresentableBy φ X).isCorepresentable
85:
86:lemma pullbackObjIsDefined_eq_top :
87:    pullbackObjIsDefined.{u} φ = ⊤ := by
88:  ext M
89:  simp only [Pi.top_apply, Prop.top_eq_true, iff_true]
90:  apply leftAdjointObjIsDefined_of_isColimit
91:    M.isColimitFreeYonedaCoproductsCokernelCofork
92:  rintro (_ | _)
93:  all_goals
94:    apply leftAdjointObjIsDefined_colimit _
95:      (fun _ ↦ pullbackObjIsDefined_free_yoneda _ _)
96:
97:instance : (pushforward.{u} φ).IsRightAdjoint :=
98:  isRightAdjoint_of_leftAdjointObjIsDefined_eq_top
99:    (pullbackObjIsDefined_eq_top φ)
100:
101:end
102:
103:section
104:
105:variable {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} D]
106:  {E : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃} E] {E' : Type u₄} [Category.{v₄} E']
107:
108:variable {F : C ⥤ D} {R : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{u}} {S : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{u}} (φ : S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R)
109:  {G : D ⥤ E} {T : Eᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{u}} (ψ : R ⟶ G.op ⋙ T)
110:
111:instance : (pushforward.{v} (F := 𝟭 C) (𝟙 S)).IsRightAdjoint :=
112:  isRightAdjoint_of_iso (pushforwardId.{v} S).symm
113:
114:variable (S) in
115:/-- The pullback by the identity morphism identifies to the identity functor of the
116:category of presheaves of modules. -/
117:noncomputable def pullbackId : pullback.{v} (F := 𝟭 C) (𝟙 S) ≅ 𝟭 _ :=
118:  ((pullbackPushforwardAdjunction.{v} (F := 𝟭 C) (𝟙 S))).leftAdjointIdIso (pushforwardId S)
119:
120:variable [(pushforward.{v} φ).IsRightAdjoint]
121:
122:section
123:
124:variable [(pushforward.{v} ψ).IsRightAdjoint]
125:
126:instance : (pushforward.{v} (F := F ⋙ G) (φ ≫ whiskerLeft F.op ψ)).IsRightAdjoint :=
127:  isRightAdjoint_of_iso (pushforwardComp.{v} φ ψ)
128:
129:/-- The composition of two pullback functors on presheaves of modules identifies
130:to the pullback for the composition. -/
131:noncomputable def pullbackComp :
132:    pullback.{v} φ ⋙ pullback.{v} ψ ≅
133:      pullback.{v} (F := F ⋙ G) (φ ≫ whiskerLeft F.op ψ) :=
134:  Adjunction.leftAdjointCompIso
135:    (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction.{v} φ) (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction.{v} ψ)
136:    (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction.{v} (F := F ⋙ G) (φ ≫ whiskerLeft F.op ψ))
137:    (pushforwardComp φ ψ)
138:
139:variable {T' : E'ᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{u}} {G' : E ⥤ E'} (ψ' : T ⟶ G'.op ⋙ T')
140:  [(pushforward.{v} ψ').IsRightAdjoint]
141:
142:lemma pullback_assoc :
143:    isoWhiskerLeft _ (pullbackComp.{v} ψ ψ') ≪≫
144:      pullbackComp.{v} (G := G ⋙ G') φ (ψ ≫ whiskerLeft G.op ψ') =
145:    (associator _ _ _).symm ≪≫ isoWhiskerRight (pullbackComp.{v} φ ψ) _ ≪≫
146:        pullbackComp.{v} (F := F ⋙ G) (φ ≫ whiskerLeft F.op ψ) ψ' :=
147:  Adjunction.leftAdjointCompIso_assoc _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ (pushforward_assoc φ ψ ψ')
148:
149:end
150:
151:lemma pullback_id_comp :
152:    pullbackComp.{v} (F := 𝟭 C) (𝟙 S) φ =
153:      isoWhiskerRight (pullbackId S) (pullback φ) ≪≫ Functor.leftUnitor _ :=
154:  Adjunction.leftAdjointCompIso_id_comp _ _ _ _ (pushforward_comp_id φ)
155:
156:lemma pullback_comp_id :
157:    pullbackComp.{v} (G := 𝟭 _) φ (𝟙 R) =
158:      isoWhiskerLeft _ (pullbackId R) ≪≫ Functor.rightUnitor _ :=
159:  Adjunction.leftAdjointCompIso_comp_id _ _ _ _ (pushforward_id_comp φ)
160:
161:end
162:
163:end PresheafOfModules

661	Def. `df:div`: "Since `D` is `T`-flat, `p_{X_T}^* \mathcal I` equals the
662	ideal of `D_{T'}`.  But, since `\mathcal I` is invertible, so is
663	`p_{X_T}^* \mathcal I`").
664	
665	For a cartesian square `sq : X' = X ×_S S'` and an epimorphism `q : E ⟶ F` of
666	`O_X`-modules with `E` quasi-coherent and `F` finitely presented and flat
667	over `S` (`Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat`), if `ker q` is locally trivial of rank
668	one then so is `ker (g'^* q)`.  Mathematical content: the short exact

13:/-!
14:# Pullback of presheaves of modules
15:
16:Let `F : C ⥤ D` be a functor, `R : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat` and `S : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat` be presheaves
17:of rings, and `φ : S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R` be a morphism of presheaves of rings,
18:we introduce the pullback functor `pullback : PresheafOfModules S ⥤ PresheafOfModules R`
19:as the left adjoint of `pushforward : PresheafOfModules R ⥤ PresheafOfModules S`.
20:The existence of this left adjoint functor is obtained under suitable universe assumptions.
21:
22:From the compatibility of `pushforward` with respect to composition, we deduce
23:similar pseudofunctor-like properties of the `pullback` functors.
24:
25:-/
26:
27:@[expose] public section
28:
29:universe v v₁ v₂ v₃ v₄ u₁ u₂ u₃ u₄ u

38:  {F : C ⥤ D} {R : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{u}} {S : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{u}} (φ : S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R)
39:  [(pushforward.{v} φ).IsRightAdjoint]
40:
41:/-- The pullback functor `PresheafOfModules S ⥤ PresheafOfModules R` induced by
42:a morphism of presheaves of rings `S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R`, defined as the left adjoint
43:functor to the pushforward, when it exists. -/
44:noncomputable def pullback : PresheafOfModules.{v} S ⥤ PresheafOfModules.{v} R :=
45:  (pushforward.{v} φ).leftAdjoint
46:
47:/-- Given a morphism of presheaves of rings `S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R`, this is the adjunction
48:between associated pullback and pushforward functors on the categories
49:of presheaves of modules. -/
50:noncomputable def pullbackPushforwardAdjunction : pullback.{v} φ ⊣ pushforward.{v} φ :=
51:  Adjunction.ofIsRightAdjoint (pushforward φ)
52:
53:/-- Given a morphism of presheaves of rings `φ : S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R`, this is the property
54:that the (partial) left adjoint functor of `pushforward φ` is defined
55:on a certain object `M : PresheafOfModules S`. -/
56:abbrev pullbackObjIsDefined : ObjectProperty (PresheafOfModules.{v} S) :=
57:  (pushforward φ).leftAdjointObjIsDefined
58:
59:end

67:`S : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat`, `R : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat` and `X : C`, the (partial) left adjoint
68:functor of `pushforward φ` is defined on the object `(free S).obj (yoneda.obj X)`:
69:this object shall be mapped to `(free R).obj (yoneda.obj (F.obj X))`. -/
70:noncomputable def pushforwardCompCoyonedaFreeYonedaCorepresentableBy (X : C) :
71:    (pushforward φ ⋙ coyoneda.obj (op ((free S).obj (yoneda.obj X)))).CorepresentableBy
72:      ((free R).obj (yoneda.obj (F.obj X))) where
73:  homEquiv {M} := freeYonedaEquiv.trans

79:    erw [Equiv.apply_symm_apply]
80:    rfl)

14:# Pullback of presheaves of modules
15:
16:Let `F : C ⥤ D` be a functor, `R : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat` and `S : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat` be presheaves
17:of rings, and `φ : S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R` be a morphism of presheaves of rings,
18:we introduce the pullback functor `pullback : PresheafOfModules S ⥤ PresheafOfModules R`
19:as the left adjoint of `pushforward : PresheafOfModules R ⥤ PresheafOfModules S`.
20:The existence of this left adjoint functor is obtained under suitable universe assumptions.
21:
22:From the compatibility of `pushforward` with respect to composition, we deduce
23:similar pseudofunctor-like properties of the `pullback` functors.
24:
25:-/
26:
27:@[expose] public section
28:
29:universe v v₁ v₂ v₃ v₄ u₁ u₂ u₃ u₄ u
30:
31:open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite Functor

37:variable {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} D]
38:  {F : C ⥤ D} {R : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{u}} {S : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{u}} (φ : S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R)
39:  [(pushforward.{v} φ).IsRightAdjoint]
40:
41:/-- The pullback functor `PresheafOfModules S ⥤ PresheafOfModules R` induced by
42:a morphism of presheaves of rings `S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R`, defined as the left adjoint
43:functor to the pushforward, when it exists. -/
44:noncomputable def pullback : PresheafOfModules.{v} S ⥤ PresheafOfModules.{v} R :=
45:  (pushforward.{v} φ).leftAdjoint
46:
47:/-- Given a morphism of presheaves of rings `S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R`, this is the adjunction
48:between associated pullback and pushforward functors on the categories
49:of presheaves of modules. -/
50:noncomputable def pullbackPushforwardAdjunction : pullback.{v} φ ⊣ pushforward.{v} φ :=
51:  Adjunction.ofIsRightAdjoint (pushforward φ)
52:
53:/-- Given a morphism of presheaves of rings `φ : S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R`, this is the property
54:that the (partial) left adjoint functor of `pushforward φ` is defined
55:on a certain object `M : PresheafOfModules S`. -/
56:abbrev pullbackObjIsDefined : ObjectProperty (PresheafOfModules.{v} S) :=
57:  (pushforward φ).leftAdjointObjIsDefined

59:end

69:this object shall be mapped to `(free R).obj (yoneda.obj (F.obj X))`. -/
70:noncomputable def pushforwardCompCoyonedaFreeYonedaCorepresentableBy (X : C) :
71:    (pushforward φ ⋙ coyoneda.obj (op ((free S).obj (yoneda.obj X)))).CorepresentableBy
72:      ((free R).obj (yoneda.obj (F.obj X))) where

79:    erw [Equiv.apply_symm_apply]

115:/-- The pullback by the identity morphism identifies to the identity functor of the
116:category of presheaves of modules. -/

127:  isRightAdjoint_of_iso (pushforwardComp.{v} φ ψ)
128:
129:/-- The composition of two pullback functors on presheaves of modules identifies
130:to the pullback for the composition. -/
131:noncomputable def pullbackComp :
132:    pullback.{v} φ ⋙ pullback.{v} ψ ≅
133:      pullback.{v} (F := F ⋙ G) (φ ≫ whiskerLeft F.op ψ) :=
134:  Adjunction.leftAdjointCompIso
135:    (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction.{v} φ) (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction.{v} ψ)
136:    (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction.{v} (F := F ⋙ G) (φ ≫ whiskerLeft F.op ψ))
137:    (pushforwardComp φ ψ)

139:variable {T' : E'ᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{u}} {G' : E ⥤ E'} (ψ' : T ⟶ G'.op ⋙ T')
140:  [(pushforward.{v} ψ').IsRightAdjoint]

142:lemma pullback_assoc :
143:    isoWhiskerLeft _ (pullbackComp.{v} ψ ψ') ≪≫
144:      pullbackComp.{v} (G := G ⋙ G') φ (ψ ≫ whiskerLeft G.op ψ') =
145:    (associator _ _ _).symm ≪≫ isoWhiskerRight (pullbackComp.{v} φ ψ) _ ≪≫
146:        pullbackComp.{v} (F := F ⋙ G) (φ ≫ whiskerLeft F.op ψ) ψ' :=
147:  Adjunction.leftAdjointCompIso_assoc _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ (pushforward_assoc φ ψ ψ')
148:
149:end

152:    pullbackComp.{v} (F := 𝟭 C) (𝟙 S) φ =
153:      isoWhiskerRight (pullbackId S) (pullback φ) ≪≫ Functor.leftUnitor _ :=
154:  Adjunction.leftAdjointCompIso_id_comp _ _ _ _ (pushforward_comp_id φ)
155:
156:lemma pullback_comp_id :
157:    pullbackComp.{v} (G := 𝟭 _) φ (𝟙 R) =
158:      isoWhiskerLeft _ (pullbackId R) ≪≫ Functor.rightUnitor _ :=
159:  Adjunction.leftAdjointCompIso_comp_id _ _ _ _ (pushforward_id_comp φ)
160:
161:end

96:/--
97:If a functor `F : C ⥤ D` preserves short exact sequences on the left-hand side, (i.e.
98:if `0 ⟶ A ⟶ B ⟶ C ⟶ 0` is exact then `0 ⟶ F(A) ⟶ F(B) ⟶ F(C)` is exact)
99:then it preserves monomorphism.
100:-/
101:lemma preservesMonomorphisms_of_preserves_shortExact_left
102:    (h : ∀ (S : ShortComplex C), S.ShortExact → (S.map F).Exact ∧ Mono (F.map S.f)) :
103:    F.PreservesMonomorphisms where
104:  preserves f := h _ { exact := exact_cokernel f } |>.2

107:/--
108:For an additive functor `F : C ⥤ D` between abelian categories, the following are equivalent:
109:- `F` preserves short exact sequences on the left-hand side, i.e. if `0 ⟶ A ⟶ B ⟶ C ⟶ 0` is exact
110:  then `0 ⟶ F(A) ⟶ F(B) ⟶ F(C)` is exact.
111:- `F` preserves exact sequences on the left-hand side, i.e. if `A ⟶ B ⟶ C` is exact where `A ⟶ B`
112:  is mono, then `F(A) ⟶ F(B) ⟶ F(C)` is exact and `F(A) ⟶ F(B)` is mono as well.
113:- `F` preserves kernels.
114:- `F` preserves finite limits.
115:-/
116:lemma preservesFiniteLimits_tfae : List.TFAE
117:    [
118:      ∀ (S : ShortComplex C), S.ShortExact → (S.map F).Exact ∧ Mono (F.map S.f),
119:      ∀ (S : ShortComplex C), S.Exact ∧ Mono S.f → (S.map F).Exact ∧ Mono (F.map S.f),
120:      ∀ ⦃X Y : C⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y), PreservesLimit (parallelPair f 0) F,
121:      PreservesFiniteLimits F
122:    ] := by
123:  tfae_have 1 → 2
124:  | hF, S, ⟨hS, hf⟩ => by
125:    have := preservesMonomorphisms_of_preserves_shortExact_left F hF
126:    refine ⟨?_, inferInstance⟩
127:    let T := ShortComplex.mk S.f (Abelian.coimage.π S.g) (Abelian.comp_coimage_π_eq_zero S.zero)
128:    let φ : T.map F ⟶ S.map F :=
129:      { τ₁ := 𝟙 _
130:        τ₂ := 𝟙 _
131:        τ₃ := F.map <| Abelian.factorThruCoimage S.g
132:        comm₂₃ := show 𝟙 _ ≫ F.map _ = F.map (cokernel.π _) ≫ _ by
133:          rw [Category.id_comp, ← F.map_comp, cokernel.π_desc] }
134:    exact (exact_iff_of_epi_of_isIso_of_mono φ).1 (hF T ⟨(S.exact_iff_exact_coimage_π).1 hS⟩).1
135:  tfae_have 2 → 3
136:  | hF, X, Y, f => by
137:    refine preservesLimit_of_preserves_limit_cone (kernelIsKernel f) ?_
138:    apply (KernelFork.isLimitMapConeEquiv _ F).2
139:    let S := ShortComplex.mk _ _ (kernel.condition f)
140:    let hS := hF S ⟨exact_kernel f, inferInstance⟩
141:    have : Mono (S.map F).f := hS.2
142:    exact hS.1.fIsKernel
143:  tfae_have 3 → 4
144:  | hF => by
145:    exact preservesFiniteLimits_of_preservesKernels F
146:  tfae_have 4 → 1
147:  | ⟨_⟩, S, hS =>
148:    (S.map F).exact_and_mono_f_iff_f_is_kernel |>.2 ⟨KernelFork.mapIsLimit _ hS.fIsKernel F⟩
149:  tfae_finish

152:    PreservesFiniteLimits F ↔
153:      ∀ (S : ShortComplex C), S.ShortExact → (S.map F).Exact ∧ Mono (F.map S.f) :=
154:  (Functor.preservesFiniteLimits_tfae F).out 3 0

157:If a functor `F : C ⥤ D` preserves exact sequences on the right-hand side (i.e.
158:if `0 ⟶ A ⟶ B ⟶ C ⟶ 0` is exact then `F(A) ⟶ F(B) ⟶ F(C) ⟶ 0` is exact),
159:then it preserves epimorphisms.

162:    (h : ∀ (S : ShortComplex C), S.ShortExact → (S.map F).Exact ∧ Epi (F.map S.g)) :

168:For an additive functor `F : C ⥤ D` between abelian categories, the following are equivalent:
169:- `F` preserves short exact sequences on the right-hand side, i.e. if `0 ⟶ A ⟶ B ⟶ C ⟶ 0` is
170:  exact then `F(A) ⟶ F(B) ⟶ F(C) ⟶ 0` is exact.
171:- `F` preserves exact sequences on the right-hand side, i.e. if `A ⟶ B ⟶ C` is exact where `B ⟶ C`
172:  is epi, then `F(A) ⟶ F(B) ⟶ F(C) ⟶ 0` is exact and `F(B) ⟶ F(C)` is epi as well.
173:- `F` preserves cokernels.
174:- `F` preserves finite colimits.
175:-/
176:lemma preservesFiniteColimits_tfae : List.TFAE
177:    [
178:      ∀ (S : ShortComplex C), S.ShortExact → (S.map F).Exact ∧ Epi (F.map S.g),
179:      ∀ (S : ShortComplex C), S.Exact ∧ Epi S.g → (S.map F).Exact ∧ Epi (F.map S.g),
180:      ∀ ⦃X Y : C⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y), PreservesColimit (parallelPair f 0) F,
181:      PreservesFiniteColimits F
182:    ] := by
183:  tfae_have 1 → 2
184:  | hF, S, ⟨hS, hf⟩ => by
185:    have := preservesEpimorphisms_of_preserves_shortExact_right F hF
186:    refine ⟨?_, inferInstance⟩
187:    let T := ShortComplex.mk (Abelian.image.ι S.f) S.g (Abelian.image_ι_comp_eq_zero S.zero)
188:    let φ : S.map F ⟶ T.map F :=
189:      { τ₁ := F.map <| Abelian.factorThruImage S.f
190:        τ₂ := 𝟙 _
191:        τ₃ := 𝟙 _
192:        comm₁₂ := show _ ≫ F.map (kernel.ι _) = F.map _ ≫ 𝟙 _ by
193:          rw [← F.map_comp, Abelian.image.fac, Category.comp_id] }
194:    exact (exact_iff_of_epi_of_isIso_of_mono φ).2 (hF T ⟨(S.exact_iff_exact_image_ι).1 hS⟩).1
195:  tfae_have 2 → 3
196:  | hF, X, Y, f => by
197:    refine preservesColimit_of_preserves_colimit_cocone (cokernelIsCokernel f) ?_
198:    apply (CokernelCofork.isColimitMapCoconeEquiv _ F).2
199:    let S := ShortComplex.mk _ _ (cokernel.condition f)
200:    let hS := hF S ⟨exact_cokernel f, inferInstance⟩
201:    have : Epi (S.map F).g := hS.2
202:    exact hS.1.gIsCokernel
203:  tfae_have 3 → 4
204:  | hF => by
205:    exact preservesFiniteColimits_of_preservesCokernels F
206:  tfae_have 4 → 1
207:  | ⟨_⟩, S, hS => (S.map F).exact_and_epi_g_iff_g_is_cokernel |>.2
208:    ⟨CokernelCofork.mapIsColimit _ hS.gIsCokernel F⟩
209:  tfae_finish

212:/--
213:For an additive functor `F : C ⥤ D` between abelian categories, the following are equivalent:
214:- `F` preserves short exact sequences, i.e. if `0 ⟶ A ⟶ B ⟶ C ⟶ 0` is exact then
215:  `0 ⟶ F(A) ⟶ F(B) ⟶ F(C) ⟶ 0` is exact.
216:- `F` preserves exact sequences, i.e. if `A ⟶ B ⟶ C` is exact then `F(A) ⟶ F(B) ⟶ F(C)` is exact.
217:- `F` preserves homology.
218:- `F` preserves both finite limits and finite colimits.
219:-/
220:lemma exact_tfae : List.TFAE
221:    [
222:      ∀ (S : ShortComplex C), S.ShortExact → (S.map F).ShortExact,
223:      ∀ (S : ShortComplex C), S.Exact → (S.map F).Exact,
224:      PreservesHomology F,
225:      PreservesFiniteLimits F ∧ PreservesFiniteColimits F
226:    ] := by
227:  tfae_have 1 → 3
228:  | hF => by
229:    refine ⟨fun {X Y} f ↦ ?_, fun {X Y} f ↦ ?_⟩
230:    · have h := (preservesFiniteLimits_tfae F |>.out 0 2 |>.1 fun S hS ↦
231:        And.intro (hF S hS).exact (hF S hS).mono_f)
232:      exact h f
233:    · have h := (preservesFiniteColimits_tfae F |>.out 0 2 |>.1 fun S hS ↦
234:        And.intro (hF S hS).exact (hF S hS).epi_g)
235:      exact h f
236:  tfae_have 2 → 1
237:  | hF, S, hS => by
238:    have : Mono (S.map F).f := exact_iff_mono _ (by simp) |>.1 <|
239:      hF (.mk (0 : 0 ⟶ S.X₁) S.f <| by simp) (exact_iff_mono _ (by simp) |>.2 hS.mono_f)
240:    have : Epi (S.map F).g := exact_iff_epi _ (by simp) |>.1 <|
241:      hF (.mk S.g (0 : S.X₃ ⟶ 0) <| by simp) (exact_iff_epi _ (by simp) |>.2 hS.epi_g)
242:    exact ⟨hF S hS.exact⟩
243:  tfae_have 3 → 4
244:  | h => ⟨preservesFiniteLimits_of_preservesHomology F,
245:      preservesFiniteColimits_of_preservesHomology F⟩
246:  tfae_have 4 → 2
247:  | ⟨h1, h2⟩, _, h => h.map F
248:  tfae_finish
249:
250:lemma preservesFiniteColimits_iff_forall_exact_map_and_epi :
251:    PreservesFiniteColimits F ↔
252:      ∀ (S : ShortComplex C), S.ShortExact → (S.map F).Exact ∧ Epi (F.map S.g) :=
253:  (Functor.preservesFiniteColimits_tfae F).out 3 0

15:Let `S` and `R` be sheaves of rings over sites `(C, J)` and `(D, K)` respectively.
16:Let `F : C ⥤ D` be a continuous functor between these sites, and
17:let `φ : S ⟶ (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{u} J K).obj R` be a morphism
18:of sheaves of rings.
19:
20:In this file, we define the pullback functor for sheaves of modules
21:`pullback.{v} φ : SheafOfModules.{v} S ⥤ SheafOfModules.{v} R`
22:that is left adjoint to `pushforward.{v} φ`. We show that it exists
23:under suitable assumptions, and prove that the pullback of (pre)sheaves of
24:modules commutes with the sheafification.
25:
26:From the compatibility of `pushforward` with respect to composition, we deduce
27:similar pseudofunctor-like properties of the `pullback` functors.
28:
29:-/
30:
31:@[expose] public section
32:
33:universe v v₁ v₂ v₃ v₄ u₁ u₂ u₃ u₄ u

35:open CategoryTheory Functor

38:
39:variable {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} D]
40:  {D' : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃} D'] {D'' : Type u₄} [Category.{v₄} D'']
41:  {J : GrothendieckTopology C} {K : GrothendieckTopology D} {F : C ⥤ D}
42:  {S : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}} {R : Sheaf K RingCat.{u}}
43:  [Functor.IsContinuous F J K]
44:  (φ : S ⟶ (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{u} J K).obj R)

48:variable [(pushforward.{v} φ).IsRightAdjoint]
49:
50:/-- The pullback functor `SheafOfModules S ⥤ SheafOfModules R` induced by
51:a morphism of sheaves of rings `S ⟶ (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{u} J K).obj R`,
52:defined as the left adjoint functor to the pushforward, when it exists. -/
53:noncomputable def pullback : SheafOfModules.{v} S ⥤ SheafOfModules.{v} R :=
54:  (pushforward.{v} φ).leftAdjoint
55:
56:/-- Given a continuous functor between sites `F`, and a morphism of sheaves of rings
57:`S ⟶ (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{u} J K).obj R`, this is the adjunction
58:between the corresponding pullback and pushforward functors on the categories
59:of sheaves of modules. -/
60:noncomputable def pullbackPushforwardAdjunction : pullback.{v} φ ⊣ pushforward.{v} φ :=
61:  Adjunction.ofIsRightAdjoint (pushforward φ)
62:
63:instance : (pullback.{v} φ).IsLeftAdjoint :=
64:  (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction φ).isLeftAdjoint

77:/-- Construction of a left adjoint to the functor `pushforward.{v} φ` by using the
78:pullback of presheaves of modules and the sheafification. -/
79:noncomputable def adjunction :
80:    (forget S ⋙ PresheafOfModules.pullback.{v} φ.hom ⋙
81:      PresheafOfModules.sheafification (R₀ := R.obj) (𝟙 R.obj)) ⊣ pushforward.{v} φ :=
82:  Adjunction.mkOfHomEquiv
83:    { homEquiv := fun F G ↦
84:        ((PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction (𝟙 R.obj)).homEquiv _ _).trans
85:            (((PresheafOfModules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction φ.hom).homEquiv F.val G.val).trans
86:              ((fullyFaithfulForget S).homEquiv (Y := (pushforward φ).obj G)).symm)
87:      homEquiv_naturality_left_symm := by
88:        intros
89:        dsimp [Functor.FullyFaithful.homEquiv]
90:        -- these erw seem difficult to remove
91:        erw [Adjunction.homEquiv_naturality_left_symm,
92:          Adjunction.homEquiv_naturality_left_symm]
93:        dsimp [pushforward_obj_val]
94:        simp only [Functor.map_comp, Category.assoc]
95:      homEquiv_naturality_right := by
96:        tauto }
97:
98:end PullbackConstruction

100:instance : (pushforward.{v} φ).IsRightAdjoint :=
101:  (PullbackConstruction.adjunction.{v} φ).isRightAdjoint

103:/-- The pullback functor on sheaves of modules can be described as a composition
104:of the forget functor to presheaves, the pullback on presheaves of modules, and
105:the sheafification functor. -/
106:noncomputable def pullbackIso :
107:    pullback.{v} φ ≅
108:      forget S ⋙ PresheafOfModules.pullback.{v} φ.hom ⋙
109:        PresheafOfModules.sheafification (R₀ := R.obj) (𝟙 R.obj) :=
110:  Adjunction.leftAdjointUniq (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction φ)
111:    (PullbackConstruction.adjunction φ)

117:/-- The pullback of (pre)sheaves of modules commutes with the sheafification. -/
118:noncomputable def sheafificationCompPullback :
119:    PresheafOfModules.sheafification (𝟙 S.obj) ⋙ pullback.{v} φ ≅
120:      PresheafOfModules.pullback.{v} φ.hom ⋙
121:        PresheafOfModules.sheafification (R₀ := R.obj) (𝟙 R.obj) :=
122:  Adjunction.leftAdjointUniq
123:    ((PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction (𝟙 S.obj)).comp
124:      (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction φ))
125:    ((PresheafOfModules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction φ.hom).comp
126:      (PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction (𝟙 R.obj)))
127:

139:noncomputable def pullbackId : pullback.{v} (F := 𝟭 C) (𝟙 S) ≅ 𝟭 _ :=

12:/-!
13:# Left exactness of functors between preadditive categories
14:
15:We show that a functor is left exact in the sense that it preserves finite limits, if it
16:preserves kernels. The dual result holds for right exact functors and cokernels.
17:
18:## Main results
19:
20:* We first derive preservation of binary product in the lemma
21:  `preservesBinaryProductsOfPreservesKernels`,
22:* then show the preservation of equalizers in `preservesEqualizerOfPreservesKernels`,
23:* and then derive the preservation of all finite limits with the usual construction.

15:
16:In this file we show that extension of scalars by a faithfully flat ring homomorphism is comonadic.
17:Then the general theory of descent implies that the pseudofunctor to `Cat` given by extension
18:of scalars has effective descent relative to faithfully flat maps (TODO).

23:"Formalizing algebraic geometry" in June 2024.

50:    (hf : f.FaithfullyFlat) : (extendScalars.{_, _, u} f).ReflectsIsomorphisms := by
51:  refine ⟨fun {M N} g h ↦ ?_⟩
52:  algebraize [f]
53:  rw [ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective] at h ⊢
54:  replace h : Function.Bijective (LinearMap.lTensor B g.hom) := h

12:/-!
13:# Pullback of sheaves of modules
14:
15:Let `S` and `R` be sheaves of rings over sites `(C, J)` and `(D, K)` respectively.
16:Let `F : C ⥤ D` be a continuous functor between these sites, and
17:let `φ : S ⟶ (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{u} J K).obj R` be a morphism
18:of sheaves of rings.
19:
20:In this file, we define the pullback functor for sheaves of modules
21:`pullback.{v} φ : SheafOfModules.{v} S ⥤ SheafOfModules.{v} R`
22:that is left adjoint to `pushforward.{v} φ`. We show that it exists
23:under suitable assumptions, and prove that the pullback of (pre)sheaves of
24:modules commutes with the sheafification.
25:
26:From the compatibility of `pushforward` with respect to composition, we deduce
27:similar pseudofunctor-like properties of the `pullback` functors.
28:
29:-/
30:
31:@[expose] public section
32:
33:universe v v₁ v₂ v₃ v₄ u₁ u₂ u₃ u₄ u
34:
35:open CategoryTheory Functor
36:
37:namespace SheafOfModules
38:
39:variable {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} D]
40:  {D' : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃} D'] {D'' : Type u₄} [Category.{v₄} D'']
41:  {J : GrothendieckTopology C} {K : GrothendieckTopology D} {F : C ⥤ D}
42:  {S : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}} {R : Sheaf K RingCat.{u}}
43:  [Functor.IsContinuous F J K]
44:  (φ : S ⟶ (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{u} J K).obj R)
45:
46:section
47:
48:variable [(pushforward.{v} φ).IsRightAdjoint]
49:
50:/-- The pullback functor `SheafOfModules S ⥤ SheafOfModules R` induced by
51:a morphism of sheaves of rings `S ⟶ (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{u} J K).obj R`,
52:defined as the left adjoint functor to the pushforward, when it exists. -/
53:noncomputable def pullback : SheafOfModules.{v} S ⥤ SheafOfModules.{v} R :=
54:  (pushforward.{v} φ).leftAdjoint
55:
56:/-- Given a continuous functor between sites `F`, and a morphism of sheaves of rings
57:`S ⟶ (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{u} J K).obj R`, this is the adjunction
58:between the corresponding pullback and pushforward functors on the categories
59:of sheaves of modules. -/
60:noncomputable def pullbackPushforwardAdjunction : pullback.{v} φ ⊣ pushforward.{v} φ :=
61:  Adjunction.ofIsRightAdjoint (pushforward φ)
62:
63:instance : (pullback.{v} φ).IsLeftAdjoint :=
64:  (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction φ).isLeftAdjoint
65:
66:end

70:variable [(PresheafOfModules.pushforward.{v} φ.hom).IsRightAdjoint]

73:namespace PullbackConstruction
74:
75:set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true in
76:set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
77:/-- Construction of a left adjoint to the functor `pushforward.{v} φ` by using the
78:pullback of presheaves of modules and the sheafification. -/
79:noncomputable def adjunction :
80:    (forget S ⋙ PresheafOfModules.pullback.{v} φ.hom ⋙
81:      PresheafOfModules.sheafification (R₀ := R.obj) (𝟙 R.obj)) ⊣ pushforward.{v} φ :=
82:  Adjunction.mkOfHomEquiv
83:    { homEquiv := fun F G ↦
84:        ((PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction (𝟙 R.obj)).homEquiv _ _).trans
85:            (((PresheafOfModules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction φ.hom).homEquiv F.val G.val).trans
86:              ((fullyFaithfulForget S).homEquiv (Y := (pushforward φ).obj G)).symm)
87:      homEquiv_naturality_left_symm := by
88:        intros
89:        dsimp [Functor.FullyFaithful.homEquiv]
90:        -- these erw seem difficult to remove
91:        erw [Adjunction.homEquiv_naturality_left_symm,
92:          Adjunction.homEquiv_naturality_left_symm]
93:        dsimp [pushforward_obj_val]
94:        simp only [Functor.map_comp, Category.assoc]
95:      homEquiv_naturality_right := by
96:        tauto }
97:
98:end PullbackConstruction
99:
100:instance : (pushforward.{v} φ).IsRightAdjoint :=
101:  (PullbackConstruction.adjunction.{v} φ).isRightAdjoint
102:
103:/-- The pullback functor on sheaves of modules can be described as a composition
104:of the forget functor to presheaves, the pullback on presheaves of modules, and
105:the sheafification functor. -/
106:noncomputable def pullbackIso :
107:    pullback.{v} φ ≅
108:      forget S ⋙ PresheafOfModules.pullback.{v} φ.hom ⋙
109:        PresheafOfModules.sheafification (R₀ := R.obj) (𝟙 R.obj) :=
110:  Adjunction.leftAdjointUniq (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction φ)
111:    (PullbackConstruction.adjunction φ)

31:- `Functor.preservesFiniteLimits_tfae`: the following are equivalent:
32:  1. for every short exact sequence `0 ⟶ A ⟶ B ⟶ C ⟶ 0`,
33:     `0 ⟶ F(A) ⟶ F(B) ⟶ F(C) ⟶ 0` is exact.
34:  2. for every exact sequence `A ⟶ B ⟶ C` where `A ⟶ B` is mono,
35:     `F(A) ⟶ F(B) ⟶ F(C)` is exact and `F(A) ⟶ F(B)` is mono.
36:  3. `F` preserves kernels.
37:  4. `F` preserves finite limits.

40:  1. for every short exact sequence `0 ⟶ A ⟶ B ⟶ C ⟶ 0`,
41:     `F(A) ⟶ F(B) ⟶ F(C) ⟶ 0` is exact.
42:  2. for every exact sequence `A ⟶ B ⟶ C` where `B ⟶ C` is epi,
43:     `F(A) ⟶ F(B) ⟶ F(C)` is exact and `F(B) ⟶ F(C)` is epi.
44:  3. `F` preserves cokernels.
45:  4. `F` preserves finite colimits.

48:  1. for every short exact sequence `0 ⟶ A ⟶ B ⟶ C ⟶ 0`,

50:  2. for every exact sequence `A ⟶ B ⟶ C`, `F(A) ⟶ F(B) ⟶ F(C)` is exact.
51:  3. `F` preserves homology.
52:  4. `F` preserves both finite limits and finite colimits.

69:/-- An additive functor which preserves homology preserves finite limits. -/
70:lemma preservesFiniteLimits_of_preservesHomology
71:    [HasFiniteProducts C] [HasKernels C] : PreservesFiniteLimits F := by
72:  have := fun {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) ↦ PreservesHomology.preservesKernel F f
73:  have : HasBinaryBiproducts C := HasBinaryBiproducts.of_hasBinaryProducts
74:  have : HasEqualizers C := Preadditive.hasEqualizers_of_hasKernels
75:  have : HasZeroObject D :=
76:    ⟨F.obj 0, by rw [IsZero.iff_id_eq_zero, ← F.map_id, id_zero, F.map_zero]⟩
77:  exact preservesFiniteLimits_of_preservesKernels F

79:/-- An additive which preserves homology preserves finite colimits. -/
80:lemma preservesFiniteColimits_of_preservesHomology
81:    [HasFiniteCoproducts C] [HasCokernels C] : PreservesFiniteColimits F := by
82:  have := fun {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) ↦ PreservesHomology.preservesCokernel F f
83:  have : HasBinaryBiproducts C := HasBinaryBiproducts.of_hasBinaryCoproducts
84:  have : HasCoequalizers C := Preadditive.hasCoequalizers_of_hasCokernels
85:  have : HasZeroObject D :=
86:    ⟨F.obj 0, by rw [IsZero.iff_id_eq_zero, ← F.map_id, id_zero, F.map_zero]⟩
87:  exact preservesFiniteColimits_of_preservesCokernels F

96:/--
97:If a functor `F : C ⥤ D` preserves short exact sequences on the left-hand side, (i.e.
98:if `0 ⟶ A ⟶ B ⟶ C ⟶ 0` is exact then `0 ⟶ F(A) ⟶ F(B) ⟶ F(C)` is exact)
99:then it preserves monomorphism.
100:-/
101:lemma preservesMonomorphisms_of_preserves_shortExact_left
102:    (h : ∀ (S : ShortComplex C), S.ShortExact → (S.map F).Exact ∧ Mono (F.map S.f)) :
103:    F.PreservesMonomorphisms where
104:  preserves f := h _ { exact := exact_cokernel f } |>.2
105:
106:set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
107:/--
108:For an additive functor `F : C ⥤ D` between abelian categories, the following are equivalent:
109:- `F` preserves short exact sequences on the left-hand side, i.e. if `0 ⟶ A ⟶ B ⟶ C ⟶ 0` is exact
110:  then `0 ⟶ F(A) ⟶ F(B) ⟶ F(C)` is exact.
111:- `F` preserves exact sequences on the left-hand side, i.e. if `A ⟶ B ⟶ C` is exact where `A ⟶ B`
112:  is mono, then `F(A) ⟶ F(B) ⟶ F(C)` is exact and `F(A) ⟶ F(B)` is mono as well.
113:- `F` preserves kernels.
114:- `F` preserves finite limits.
115:-/
116:lemma preservesFiniteLimits_tfae : List.TFAE
117:    [
118:      ∀ (S : ShortComplex C), S.ShortExact → (S.map F).Exact ∧ Mono (F.map S.f),
119:      ∀ (S : ShortComplex C), S.Exact ∧ Mono S.f → (S.map F).Exact ∧ Mono (F.map S.f),
120:      ∀ ⦃X Y : C⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y), PreservesLimit (parallelPair f 0) F,
121:      PreservesFiniteLimits F
122:    ] := by
123:  tfae_have 1 → 2
124:  | hF, S, ⟨hS, hf⟩ => by
125:    have := preservesMonomorphisms_of_preserves_shortExact_left F hF
126:    refine ⟨?_, inferInstance⟩
127:    let T := ShortComplex.mk S.f (Abelian.coimage.π S.g) (Abelian.comp_coimage_π_eq_zero S.zero)
128:    let φ : T.map F ⟶ S.map F :=
129:      { τ₁ := 𝟙 _
130:        τ₂ := 𝟙 _
131:        τ₃ := F.map <| Abelian.factorThruCoimage S.g
132:        comm₂₃ := show 𝟙 _ ≫ F.map _ = F.map (cokernel.π _) ≫ _ by
133:          rw [Category.id_comp, ← F.map_comp, cokernel.π_desc] }
134:    exact (exact_iff_of_epi_of_isIso_of_mono φ).1 (hF T ⟨(S.exact_iff_exact_coimage_π).1 hS⟩).1
135:  tfae_have 2 → 3
136:  | hF, X, Y, f => by
137:    refine preservesLimit_of_preserves_limit_cone (kernelIsKernel f) ?_
138:    apply (KernelFork.isLimitMapConeEquiv _ F).2
139:    let S := ShortComplex.mk _ _ (kernel.condition f)
140:    let hS := hF S ⟨exact_kernel f, inferInstance⟩
141:    have : Mono (S.map F).f := hS.2
142:    exact hS.1.fIsKernel
143:  tfae_have 3 → 4
144:  | hF => by
145:    exact preservesFiniteLimits_of_preservesKernels F
146:  tfae_have 4 → 1
147:  | ⟨_⟩, S, hS =>
148:    (S.map F).exact_and_mono_f_iff_f_is_kernel |>.2 ⟨KernelFork.mapIsLimit _ hS.fIsKernel F⟩
149:  tfae_finish
150:
151:lemma preservesFiniteLimits_iff_forall_exact_map_and_mono :
152:    PreservesFiniteLimits F ↔
153:      ∀ (S : ShortComplex C), S.ShortExact → (S.map F).Exact ∧ Mono (F.map S.f) :=
154:  (Functor.preservesFiniteLimits_tfae F).out 3 0

156:/--
157:If a functor `F : C ⥤ D` preserves exact sequences on the right-hand side (i.e.
158:if `0 ⟶ A ⟶ B ⟶ C ⟶ 0` is exact then `F(A) ⟶ F(B) ⟶ F(C) ⟶ 0` is exact),
159:then it preserves epimorphisms.
160:-/
161:lemma preservesEpimorphisms_of_preserves_shortExact_right
162:    (h : ∀ (S : ShortComplex C), S.ShortExact → (S.map F).Exact ∧ Epi (F.map S.g)) :
163:    F.PreservesEpimorphisms where
164:  preserves f := h _ { exact := exact_kernel f } |>.2
165:
166:set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
167:/--
168:For an additive functor `F : C ⥤ D` between abelian categories, the following are equivalent:
169:- `F` preserves short exact sequences on the right-hand side, i.e. if `0 ⟶ A ⟶ B ⟶ C ⟶ 0` is
170:  exact then `F(A) ⟶ F(B) ⟶ F(C) ⟶ 0` is exact.
171:- `F` preserves exact sequences on the right-hand side, i.e. if `A ⟶ B ⟶ C` is exact where `B ⟶ C`
172:  is epi, then `F(A) ⟶ F(B) ⟶ F(C) ⟶ 0` is exact and `F(B) ⟶ F(C)` is epi as well.
173:- `F` preserves cokernels.
174:- `F` preserves finite colimits.
175:-/
176:lemma preservesFiniteColimits_tfae : List.TFAE
177:    [
178:      ∀ (S : ShortComplex C), S.ShortExact → (S.map F).Exact ∧ Epi (F.map S.g),
179:      ∀ (S : ShortComplex C), S.Exact ∧ Epi S.g → (S.map F).Exact ∧ Epi (F.map S.g),
180:      ∀ ⦃X Y : C⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y), PreservesColimit (parallelPair f 0) F,
181:      PreservesFiniteColimits F
182:    ] := by
183:  tfae_have 1 → 2
184:  | hF, S, ⟨hS, hf⟩ => by
185:    have := preservesEpimorphisms_of_preserves_shortExact_right F hF
186:    refine ⟨?_, inferInstance⟩
187:    let T := ShortComplex.mk (Abelian.image.ι S.f) S.g (Abelian.image_ι_comp_eq_zero S.zero)
188:    let φ : S.map F ⟶ T.map F :=
189:      { τ₁ := F.map <| Abelian.factorThruImage S.f
190:        τ₂ := 𝟙 _
191:        τ₃ := 𝟙 _
192:        comm₁₂ := show _ ≫ F.map (kernel.ι _) = F.map _ ≫ 𝟙 _ by
193:          rw [← F.map_comp, Abelian.image.fac, Category.comp_id] }
194:    exact (exact_iff_of_epi_of_isIso_of_mono φ).2 (hF T ⟨(S.exact_iff_exact_image_ι).1 hS⟩).1
195:  tfae_have 2 → 3
196:  | hF, X, Y, f => by
197:    refine preservesColimit_of_preserves_colimit_cocone (cokernelIsCokernel f) ?_
198:    apply (CokernelCofork.isColimitMapCoconeEquiv _ F).2
199:    let S := ShortComplex.mk _ _ (cokernel.condition f)
200:    let hS := hF S ⟨exact_cokernel f, inferInstance⟩
201:    have : Epi (S.map F).g := hS.2
202:    exact hS.1.gIsCokernel
203:  tfae_have 3 → 4
204:  | hF => by
205:    exact preservesFiniteColimits_of_preservesCokernels F
206:  tfae_have 4 → 1
207:  | ⟨_⟩, S, hS => (S.map F).exact_and_epi_g_iff_g_is_cokernel |>.2
208:    ⟨CokernelCofork.mapIsColimit _ hS.gIsCokernel F⟩
209:  tfae_finish
210:
211:set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
212:/--
213:For an additive functor `F : C ⥤ D` between abelian categories, the following are equivalent:
214:- `F` preserves short exact sequences, i.e. if `0 ⟶ A ⟶ B ⟶ C ⟶ 0` is exact then
215:  `0 ⟶ F(A) ⟶ F(B) ⟶ F(C) ⟶ 0` is exact.
216:- `F` preserves exact sequences, i.e. if `A ⟶ B ⟶ C` is exact then `F(A) ⟶ F(B) ⟶ F(C)` is exact.
217:- `F` preserves homology.
218:- `F` preserves both finite limits and finite colimits.
219:-/
220:lemma exact_tfae : List.TFAE
221:    [
222:      ∀ (S : ShortComplex C), S.ShortExact → (S.map F).ShortExact,
223:      ∀ (S : ShortComplex C), S.Exact → (S.map F).Exact,
224:      PreservesHomology F,
225:      PreservesFiniteLimits F ∧ PreservesFiniteColimits F
226:    ] := by
227:  tfae_have 1 → 3
228:  | hF => by
229:    refine ⟨fun {X Y} f ↦ ?_, fun {X Y} f ↦ ?_⟩
230:    · have h := (preservesFiniteLimits_tfae F |>.out 0 2 |>.1 fun S hS ↦
231:        And.intro (hF S hS).exact (hF S hS).mono_f)
232:      exact h f
233:    · have h := (preservesFiniteColimits_tfae F |>.out 0 2 |>.1 fun S hS ↦
234:        And.intro (hF S hS).exact (hF S hS).epi_g)
235:      exact h f
236:  tfae_have 2 → 1
237:  | hF, S, hS => by
238:    have : Mono (S.map F).f := exact_iff_mono _ (by simp) |>.1 <|
239:      hF (.mk (0 : 0 ⟶ S.X₁) S.f <| by simp) (exact_iff_mono _ (by simp) |>.2 hS.mono_f)
240:    have : Epi (S.map F).g := exact_iff_epi _ (by simp) |>.1 <|
241:      hF (.mk S.g (0 : S.X₃ ⟶ 0) <| by simp) (exact_iff_epi _ (by simp) |>.2 hS.epi_g)
242:    exact ⟨hF S hS.exact⟩
243:  tfae_have 3 → 4
244:  | h => ⟨preservesFiniteLimits_of_preservesHomology F,
245:      preservesFiniteColimits_of_preservesHomology F⟩
246:  tfae_have 4 → 2
247:  | ⟨h1, h2⟩, _, h => h.map F
248:  tfae_finish
249:
250:lemma preservesFiniteColimits_iff_forall_exact_map_and_epi :
251:    PreservesFiniteColimits F ↔
252:      ∀ (S : ShortComplex C), S.ShortExact → (S.map F).Exact ∧ Epi (F.map S.g) :=
253:  (Functor.preservesFiniteColimits_tfae F).out 3 0
254:
255:end
